title: Roll puff pastry into an even 3 mm sheet, both hands keeping the spacer-ring pin level, without rolling off the ends
instruction: Roll this puff pastry out into a 3 mm sheet at least 20 cm long.
context: Bakers (O*NET 51-3011.00: roll, knead, cut or shape dough to form pie crusts, tarts and other products) roll pastry to a set thickness many times a shift. Spacer rings on the pin's barrel set the thickness only while both rings ride on the board, so the pin is driven level by both handles: with one end lifted it leaves a wedge. Dough springs back, so it takes several passes. Bakers roll from the middle out to each end and stop short of the edge (America's Test Kitchen: roll outward from center to edge; Food Republic on puff pastry: flattened or crimped edges have difficulty rising): a pin rolled off the end presses the cut edge thin and seals the layers, so that edge will not rise. Uneven pastry bakes unevenly and is scrapped.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. Full scale. An oiled maple pastry board (mid brown, darker than the table) 31 cm deep (x) by 28 cm across (y) and 1.5 cm thick lies fixed on the table, spanning x 14 to 45 and y -14 to 14, top at z 1.5, lightly floured (a wooden pin slides on it with friction 0.15 static, 0.10 dynamic). On it lies a chilled block of puff pastry 6.5 cm (x) by 20 cm (y) by 1.0 cm thick (130 mL, about 130 g), centered at x 30, y 0. Behind the pastry, a wooden rolling pin lies in its rest with its axis along y at x 41.5, z 5: 43 cm overall and 450 g, a barrel 5 cm across and 26 cm long (y -13 to 13), a blue silicone spacer ring 5.6 cm across (3 mm proud of the barrel) and 1.5 cm wide on each end of the barrel (|y| 11.5 to 13), and dark wooden handles 2.5 cm across and 8.5 cm long (|y| 13 to 21.5). The rest is two fixed dark wooden cradles on the table just outside the board's sides, one under the outer end of each handle (|y| 19.5 to 21.5, 4.5 cm deep in x, centered at x 41.5), each a block whose top carries the handle at z 3.75 with a 5 mm lip 1 cm tall in front of and behind the handle; in it the rings are 7 mm above the board. The pastry is modeled: it has no collider, and is shown as 1 cm slabs as thick as the pastry there, colored by thickness (cream over 6.5 mm, golds down to golden at 2.5 to 3.5 mm on spec, tan and dark brown below).
scoring: Scored on the final state, which must hold 1 s. The pastry is read on a 1 cm grid: 20 strips 1 cm wide along x. A slice of pastry the pin's barrel rolls across, with the barrel's lowest line below its top, is pressed to the gap plus half its excess (the gap is the barrel's height above the board there: 3 mm with both rings on the board, more on the side of a lifted end), lengthening the sheet, but only while both handles are held (the barrel turns on its axle between them); four presses bring the 10 mm block within 0.5 mm of 3 mm. 1.0 if every strip is at least 20 cm long (the floor of a 20 cm square pan), at least 90 % of the sheet's cells are 3 mm within 0.5 mm (the ring's 3 mm plus half a millimeter of springback; 10 % is the 1 cm trimmed off each end), no end was rolled over, the pin is set down level within 3 degrees (back in its rest, or on its rings on the board, within 5 mm), every tool point and pad tip is 1 cm clear of the pin, and both arms are back home and still (each tool point within 3 cm of where it started); 0.9 if not home. 0.5 if, with the same pin and end conditions, every strip is at least 18 cm long (one pass to go) but the sheet is short of 20 cm or under 90 % on spec. 0 if an end was rolled over (the barrel more than 5 mm past it while pressing, two steps in a row: its last 1 cm is pressed to 1.8 mm and sealed, latched), if pastry was pressed with a tool point or pad tip within 1 cm of the barrel or rings (two steps in a row: the barrel stops turning, skids and tears it; latched), any strip is shorter than 18 cm (nothing done, one or two passes, or a wedge from a tilted pin, whose high side stays thick and short), or the pin is still held or not set down. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 0.9, 1.0. In a real trial, photograph the sheet over a 1 cm grid transparency and measure each long edge and the middle with a ruler; read thickness with a needle depth gauge at the center of each 2 cm square (about 100 points); an end under 2 mm or pressed flat and shiny is sealed.
reset_notes: The pastry is consumed: each real trial needs a fresh block of chilled store-bought puff pastry, cut and pressed into 6.5 x 20 x 1 cm (130 g), set centered at x 30, y 0, 20 to 30 minutes out of the fridge (about 18 C). Re-flour the board, put the pin back in its rest (axis along y), check both rings are on the barrel ends.
fidelity: The pastry is a scored model with no collider: the pin rides on its rings and the kit presses what the barrel rolls over. Springback (half the excess per pass), contact reach and the sealed edge's 1.8 mm are estimates to measure. The pin slides instead of its barrel turning on an axle, so rolling counts only with both handles held and a hand on the barrel tears the pastry. Arm press force is not modeled; the sheet lengthens only along x.
